拿到了百花奖最佳女主角，卫诗雅的反应很有意思。

​跟别的女演员不一样，她第一反应不是惊喜，而是无措。她慌里慌张地起身，整个人看起来是懵的，紧张、激动、尴尬全写在了脸上。

​看来这次百花奖果然是爆冷，她只身一人来内地参加典礼，估计以为自己只是来陪跑的，没想到能走到上台发表获奖感言这一步。

​发言的时候甚至能看到她被缝了五十多针的嘴唇都没好利索，礼服也是简简单单的，没有过多的准备，但努力让自己说出口的普通话能让大家听懂，也是怪可爱的。

​听说她主演的这部电影《破地狱》真的很好看，是妥妥的实力派，你们看过吗？感受如何？

text:
刚刚，一篇可能会引起大模型圈地震的论文发表了！

研究人员第一次系统性地从 OpenAI、Anthropic、Google 的闭源模型里，大规模“偷”出了真正的隐藏思维链。

然后，他们顺手拿这些思维链去研究了 Kimi K3、GLM-5.2、DeepSeek 等一批开源模型。

结果非常有意思。

01｜原来闭源模型的 CoT，真的可以被“偷”出来

现在 OpenAI、Anthropic、Google 都越来越不愿意把完整思维链交给用户。

原因也很好理解：最终答案可以抄，真正值钱的是模型“怎么想”。

一旦完整 CoT 被批量拿走，就可以直接拿去做蒸馏，训练自己的模型。

所以现在很多 API 的做法，是把模型的 reasoning 加密以后返回给客户端。你看不到内容，但下一轮请求可以把这坨加密数据再交回模型，让它继续思考。

结果研究者发现了一个很离谱的漏洞：

这些加密思维链，在同一家厂商的不同用户、Session，甚至不同模型之间，居然可以互相兼容。

于是攻击方法简单得有点荒谬：

让最强模型思考 → 拿到加密 CoT → 扔给同厂更弱、更容易越狱的模型 → 让小模型把它解出来。

比如 Claude Opus 4.8 的隐藏思维链，可以交给 Haiku 去“念”出来。

你甚至不需要攻破 Opus，找它的小弟Haiku就行。

论文最终在 Claude、GPT、Gemini 三套 API 上都实现了隐藏 reasoning 的提取，等于直接绕过了厂商原本用来防止 CoT 蒸馏的那层保护。

text:
香港娱乐圈终于出了个可怕的演员

那就是卫诗雅

不是她拍戏嘴巴缝了50多针，而是她花了一年的时间去全身心学习殡葬非遗手艺，这种正式拍摄前先行沉浸式体验角色，在咱们内娱，仿佛是上辈子的事了。

卫诗雅在拍《破.地狱》这个片子时，真的是经历了重重困难。

第一关是她需要学习香港传统喃这个手艺，常年是传男不传女的，根本没有师傅搭理她。她愣是费劲心思，整整花了三个月，找到两位愿意向她传授丧葬法器动作的师傅，把他们两个的教学拼在一块，才算凑完整了整个仪轨。

第二关是想掌握这套仪式，要熟记古法经文，法器的摆放走位，跳火堆流程，她本身肢体并不协调，愣是死磕九个月，形成了肌肉记忆。同时为了和角色匹配，她需要有好的体能，专门用了一年，请了私教一对一培训。

第三关是香港人多殡仪馆很忙，只有正月初一，清明和重阳三天供她观摩拍摄，这就意味着这三天她得熬大夜压缩拍摄时长，更不用说长期走访殡仪馆和丧葬铺子，观察从业者的习惯，神态和微表情。

说实话，就像卫诗雅这种沉浸式体验派，内心不抑郁是不可能的，她为了角色，拼了！

text:
Quick tip when using /to-tickets:

1. Think about how big the task is
2. Approximate how many tokens you'd need to spend to complete it (this takes experience - higher estimates are safer)
3. Divide that total by 150k (the approx smart zone of SOTA agents)
4. That gives you the number of tickets you need.

A big refactor might be 1M tokens. That's 6.66 smart zones, so 7 tickets.

Nice heuristic if you're not sure.

text:
这个提醒我很认同，因为我自己平时也经常用这种「对抗式审计」。

通常是 Fable 先写代码，再让 GPT-5.6 Sol 单独 Review，专门去找潜在的 Bug、边界问题和遗漏。大多数时候确实能发现不少问题。

但我也遇到过另一种情况：Review Agent 只是觉得某段代码「看起来有问题」，实际上原来的实现是对的。结果顺着它的建议改下去，反而把正确代码改坏了。

所以现在我会更在意 Review 给出的结论能不能被测试或者被其他证据验证。

现在想让两个模型互相挑错很容易，难的是判断这次修改到底有没有让系统变得更好。

quotedTweet.text:
when you ask an LLM to audit your code, it is essentially answering: "does this code have some pattern that *looks like* a bug?" this is important because many things can "look like" a bug, while still being correct. and "fixing" something that is correct will make it incorrect.

I've ran an experiment where I set up a loop:
- GPT 5.6 Pro audits an algorithm
- Fable 5 to fixes the bugs GPT found
- repeat
with a catch: the algorithm was *already correct* (literally, proven so). the result is complete degradation: in the first iterations, the correct algorithm becomes incorrect. in the next iterations, the (now incorrect) algorithm gets patched. but the patches introduce new cases and bugs. this keeps going until the code is destroyed.

so, a naive loop where a model audits its own code ("adversarially") and then fixes it will lead to failure. of course, as LLMs get smarter, *looks like* a bug will converge to being equivalent, in practically 100% of the cases, to finding a real bug. I think we're very close to that, and it will be interesting when the error rate is so low that these loops start working. but, as of 2026, we're not quite there yet

- Fable 5 to fixes the bugs GPT found
- repeat
with a catch: the algorithm was *already correct* (literally, proven so). the result is complete degradation: in the first iterations, the correct algorithm becomes incorrect. in the next iterations, the (now incorrect) algorithm gets patched. but the patches introduce new cases and bugs. this keeps going until the code is destroyed.

so, a naive loop where a model audits its own code ("adversarially") and then fixes it will lead to failure. of course, as LLMs get smarter, *looks like* a bug will converge to being equivalent, in practically 100% of the cases, to finding a real bug. I think we're very close to that, and it will be interesting when the error rate is so low that these loops start working. but, as of 2026, we're not quite there yet

text:
😤WTF？！所以穷人孩子一直穷，富人孩子一直富？？

最近刷到个视频，一个亿万富翁，让十来岁的女儿当场打电话向陌生人推销，还真成交了，那份掌控感超过八成成年人。

这人叫 Grant Cardone，汽车销售出身，做成了亿万富翁，还上过一档综艺：隐去身份、只带 100 美金和一辆皮卡，90 天从零干出一家百万美元公司（Discovery 的《卧底亿万富翁》）。就那种把"搞钱"刻进骨子里的人。

后来他专门录了条1h视频，当面把整套财富思维一条条教给女儿。我全听完了，挑4个自己最有共鸣的和大家共勉：

一、听建议，只听比你强的人的。
他说这辈子踩的一个大坑，就是听了太多人的建议；回头复盘，真正有用的全来自比他更有结果的人。

这点我太有体感！你听菜鸡的建议，只能变成菜鸡；你听你爸的，顶多变成你爸。
同级朋友和没搞过钱的父母，能给你的就是他们认知的天花板，而那个天花板，大概率还没你高。

二、钱，跟着注意力走。
你东西做得再好，没人知道你，就没人买，市场没义务来发现你。他后来拼命做内容、上电视、搞播客，就是想明白了：不会传播的人只能一遍遍费力自证，攥着注意力的人机会自己找上门。
咱们搞AI开发，Build in public不也是为了争夺注意力吗？

三、别老实站在队伍最后。

这个例子我当场醍醐灌顶：他带家人去演唱会买吃的，队排老长。他没排，直接找到排最前面那位，说我帮你付钱、你顺手帮我带两份。
一句话，省下一小时。他没挤走任何人，就是做了笔双方都划算的交换。

虽然我觉得这多少助长了黄牛产业hhh，但确实想要破局，就不能默认，"自己慢慢耗时间"是解决问题的唯一办法。

四、别跟所有人打架，要挑跟谁打。

只要你开始公开表达、有了成绩，批评一定来。但有些人骂你，纯粹想借走你的注意力，你一回应，就把流量、时间、情绪白送给他了。
对那些伤不到你、也没影响力的人，最好的回应就是不回应；只有当对方传播力够大、或真能砸你饭碗时，无视才失效。

最后、
女儿问他：如果只能留三条人生建议，最想让我记住啥？他几乎没想就脱口而出：
一，嫁对人。
二，别有太多朋友。
三，一定要搞懂钱。

听着是婚姻、人际、财富三件事，其实是同一件：你这辈子过成什么样，很大程度就取决于你把谁放进核心圈、把时间给谁、把钱怎么用。

听完最大的感受是：普通人家总想帮孩子挡住现实，让他单纯、晚点碰人性和利益；
这种家庭反过来——越早让孩子看懂真实世界怎么运转，他将来越不容易被别人定的规则收割。

result.text:
😤WTF？！所以穷人孩子一直穷，富人孩子一直富？？

最近刷到个视频，一个亿万富翁，让十来岁的女儿当场打电话向陌生人推销，还真成交了，那份掌控感超过八成成年人。

这人叫 Grant Cardone，汽车销售出身，做成了亿万富翁，还上过一档综艺：隐去身份、只带 100 美金和一辆皮卡，90 天从零干出一家百万美元公司（Discovery 的《卧底亿万富翁》）。就那种把"搞钱"刻进骨子里的人。

后来他专门录了条1h视频，当面把整套财富思维一条条教给女儿。我全听完了，挑4个自己最有共鸣的和大家共勉：

一、听建议，只听比你强的人的。
他说这辈子踩的一个大坑，就是听了太多人的建议；回头复盘，真正有用的全来自比他更有结果的人。

这点我太有体感！你听菜鸡的建议，只能变成菜鸡；你听你爸的，顶多变成你爸。
同级朋友和没搞过钱的父母，能给你的就是他们认知的天花板，而那个天花板，大概率还没你高。

二、钱，跟着注意力走。
你东西做得再好，没人知道你，就没人买，市场没义务来发现你。他后来拼命做内容、上电视、搞播客，就是想明白了：不会传播的人只能一遍遍费力自证，攥着注意力的人机会自己找上门。
咱们搞AI开发，Build in public不也是为了争夺注意力吗？

三、别老实站在队伍最后。

这个例子我当场醍醐灌顶：他带家人去演唱会买吃的，队排老长。他没排，直接找到排最前面那位，说我帮你付钱、你顺手帮我带两份。
一句话，省下一小时。他没挤走任何人，就是做了笔双方都划算的交换。

虽然我觉得这多少助长了黄牛产业hhh，但确实想要破局，就不能默认，"自己慢慢耗时间"是解决问题的唯一办法。

四、别跟所有人打架，要挑跟谁打。

只要你开始公开表达、有了成绩，批评一定来。但有些人骂你，纯粹想借走你的注意力，你一回应，就把流量、时间、情绪白送给他了。
对那些伤不到你、也没影响力的人，最好的回应就是不回应；只有当对方传播力够大、或真能砸你饭碗时，无视才失效。

最后、
女儿问他：如果只能留三条人生建议，最想让我记住啥？他几乎没想就脱口而出：
一，嫁对人。
二，别有太多朋友。
三，一定要搞懂钱。

听着是婚姻、人际、财富三件事，其实是同一件：你这辈子过成什么样，很大程度就取决于你把谁放进核心圈、把时间给谁、把钱怎么用。

听完最大的感受是：普通人家总想帮孩子挡住现实，让他单纯、晚点碰人性和利益；
这种家庭反过来——越早让孩子看懂真实世界怎么运转，他将来越不容易被别人定的规则收割。

https://t.co/xfgSdZsbDN

text:
只买成交额最高的股票能否跑赢大盘？

规则：每天按成交额给全市场排序，谁连续五天排第一就全仓买谁，被顶下去就换。20年美股，4360万根日线。

如果只看结果：年化19.01%，同期标普500才9.40%。

把区间切开看，前十年年化26.3%，标普5.5%；后十年12.2%，标普13.5%，纳指19.9%。最近三年是负的，同期标普年化19.5%。钱全是2012年以前赚的。

再去看它到底买了什么。20年里有52.6%的时间是满仓苹果，把苹果整个拿掉，年化从19%掉到7.23%。

最大的回撤几乎都来自特斯拉。持有1129天，仅次于苹果。把它拿掉，收益反而从19%涨到22.4%。

text:
你用 Codex 跑大项目的时候，token 其实有一大块是白烧的。

不是模型笨，是你喂给它的东西太脏了。

每次 git diff、git status、测试日志、cat 文件——这些命令输出里大半都是 Codex 根本不需要的内容。但每一行都在吃你的 token。

RTK（Rust Token Killer）就是干这件事的。

它在终端输出进入 Codex 之前，自动压缩掉冗余部分。官方数据：常见命令输出能砍掉 60-90%。

单次调用可能感觉不出来。但 Codex 在大项目里连续跑几个小时，不断读 diff、跑测试、看日志——累计省下的 token 非常可观。

本质上不是让 Codex 少干活。
是别让它把 token 烧在垃圾上下文上。

🔗链接：
https://t.co/oFlbIwSg79

result.text:
你用 Codex 跑大项目的时候，token 其实有一大块是白烧的。

不是模型笨，是你喂给它的东西太脏了。

每次 git diff、git status、测试日志、cat 文件——这些命令输出里大半都是 Codex 根本不需要的内容。但每一行都在吃你的 token。

RTK（Rust Token Killer）就是干这件事的。

它在终端输出进入 Codex 之前，自动压缩掉冗余部分。官方数据：常见命令输出能砍掉 60-90%。

单次调用可能感觉不出来。但 Codex 在大项目里连续跑几个小时，不断读 diff、跑测试、看日志——累计省下的 token 非常可观。

本质上不是让 Codex 少干活。
是别让它把 token 烧在垃圾上下文上。

A Note to Our Users

Manus will soon resume operating as an independent company.

As part of this transition and to comply with regulatory requirements in specific jurisdictions, some users will need to back-up their data before 7:59 a.m. on August 23, 2026 (SGT) and then begin restoration starting from 8:00 a.m on August 25, 2026 (SGT) to ensure normal usage.

More information can be found in the blog post and we’ve provided detailed guides, including to understand if you’re affected, in our Help Center

For affected users, these are the key details:

We’ll notify you by email and in the Manus app. If you signed up with an Apple ID or Facebook account, please check your in-app notifications.

Back up your data from now until August 23 (SGT) before 7:59 a.m. You can back up more than once, you can create new data after backing up, just run it again.  

Starting from 8:00 a.m. on August 25 (SGT), the restoration portal will open. Restore your data and pick up right where you left off.

Affected users will not be charged during the transition, and we will be providing welcome back bonuses.

If your account is not affected, you don’t need to do anything - keep using Manus as usual. You’ll get an in-app notification confirming this.

For those affected, we know this is disruptive and we’re sorry for the inconvenience. Supporting you through it is our top priority. In addition to the full guides in the Help Center, our customer service team is ready to help 24/7 with any questions.

As we look ahead, we couldn’t be more excited by the future. We’re preparing a series of new features that will push the boundaries of what’s possible for general AI agents once again.

Thank you for being with us as we go through this process together. The best is still ahead.

text:
What happens when “giving patients what they want” isn’t the same thing as giving patients what they need?

That’s a conversation I’ve been having for years. In my TEDx talk, “How Patient Satisfaction Scores Affect Healthcare,” I explored the uncomfortable reality that our pursuit of patient satisfaction can sometimes incentivize the wrong things and ultimately harm the very patients we’re trying to serve.

So I’m especially excited to take that conversation forward this September at Becker’s 11th Annual Health IT + Digital Health + RCM Conference in Chicago, where I’ll be joining an incredible panel to discuss “How to Meet Rising Consumer Experience Expectations in Healthcare”. I am honored to share the stage with:

• Mohamed Abdelaziz, MD, MPH — Bon Secours Mercy Health
• @Scott_Paddock — Silver Cross Hospital
• @AMelville — Northwestern Medicine
• Ann-Marie Yap , CHCIO , CDH-E — Stanford Health Care and School of Medicine
• Moderated by Sophie Eydis, Assistant Editor, @BeckersHR 

The patient experience matters enormously but is NOT necessarily the same as patient satisfaction. Healthcare consumers absolutely deserve better access, better communication, better technology, better transparency, and systems designed around their needs.

But excellent healthcare also means being willing to say no when no is the safer answer. That tension between consumer expectations and clinical responsibility is exactly where the conversation gets interesting...and this panel is going to get spicy!🔥

🎥 Watch the TEDx talk that started it all: https://t.co/AixgnT1QAx

text:
I think yesterday’s $500B AI financing announcement is extremely bullish for the neoclouds.

My biggest takeaway: the AI infrastructure buildout is becoming too large to be funded entirely through traditional hyperscaler capex.

There is an enormous amount of outside capital looking for exposure to AI infrastructure, and that creates another source of funding for compute, GPUs, power and data centers.

That matters for neoclouds because capital has arguably been one of the biggest constraints on how quickly they can scale.

My top pick remains $NBIS.

They already have the demand, NVIDIA relationship, infrastructure pipeline and a clear path to multiple gigawatts of capacity. If AI infrastructure financing continues moving in this direction, I think the market will eventually have to rethink how quickly NBIS can scale.

Still my highest-conviction neocloud. 

Looking forward to their earnings call tomorrow morning.

text:
Your contract review agent can read an NDA and summarize the key terms. But ask it "what are the risky clauses?" and you get a different answer every time.

Neither gets solved by a bigger model.

Here's a deep dive of the Box AI Extract NDA risk workflow. 

The agent calls POST /2.0/ai/extract_structured with a fixed five-field schema: governing law, term, termination, confidentiality period, liability cap. Confidence scores and source references included. A transparent rule set scores each clause automatically. 

The Deal Risk Summary saves back to Box as a companion file alongside the source document. Same output shape every time, regardless of how the document is written.

Extract, don't prompt.

text:
I’m a moderatly good person —great friend, dog lover, all-around amazing. It's hard to tell you how good I am because I don't want to brag. I’m known for my incredible wisdom and knowledge. People seek my wisdom and knowledge from miles around. I help the downtrodden, comfort the uncomfortable, give great advice nobody asked for, and I once got a Wi-Fi password right on the first try. My smile has been known to cure minor ailments, and I part the Red Sea on Tuesdays. After all that, I’m extremely humble. I honestly don’t know why God’s been so good to me. Anyway, I’m a very good man, I've even been called the man of all men. Yes I'm a good man, just ask me. By best attribute is I’m extremely humble.

Just so we’re clear — I’m bad to the bone. I don’t walk, I strut. I don’t ask for Wi-Fi passwords, I demand them. My dog doesn’t walk me, I allow him to accompany me. I give unsolicited advice so good, even your therapist takes notes. I once parallel parked on the first try and didn’t even brag… out loud.
But for real, I’m just a regular guy who loves people and . I’m Happy to help whenever I can. Seriously though, the best thing about me is I’m so humble.
Humility is my number one attribut

I’m not saying I’m a superhero, but have you ever seen me and Superman in the same room? Exactly. I’m the kind of guy who can read an entire 3-hour sermon transcript in 30 seconds flat and still have time to teach my dog how to use the iPad. I give unsolicited life advice so profound it belongs on a billboard, and I once solved a rubik's cube just by staring at it intensely. But despite my overwhelming brilliance and the fact that local universities are begging me to teach a class on advanced napping, the absolute best thing about me is my staggering, unmatched humility. I am easily the most humble man in human history—just ask anyone, they’ll tell you I’m a legend at it."

Well, I better stop here before I get carried away.
It always did work on job applications though.

text:
Storytelling also remains unsolved for another fundamental reason: taste. 

What is taste? It is the ability to combine suspense, playfulness, pacing, and restraint to reveal the right information at exactly the right moment. The interplay of these qualities is what narrative theory has long recognized as the foundation of compelling storytelling. 

This became especially apparent when our first research models outperformed OpenAI's and Anthropic's models by 9× on storytelling evaluations. That result was not an accident. 

Frontier models are optimized to be predictable. They should be. Their objective is to answer as truthfully as possible. Storytelling, however, requires the opposite. Great stories deliberately withhold answers, build tension, surprise the audience, and reveal information only when it has the greatest emotional impact. 

That is why storytelling remains an unsolved problem. It is not simply a challenge of generating coherent text. It is a challenge of narrative taste.

🐻 $MU bears are focused on when margins peak.

📈 Margin peak ≠ earnings peak.

I’m focused on where margins settle.

UBS estimates ex-HBM DRAM gross margins could peak near 95%, then remain around 88% into 2029. HBM margins could remain near 72–78%, while HBM grows toward 12% of DRAM bits.

That isn’t a collapse.

It’s a new, structurally higher margin plateau.

From there, earnings increasingly become a volume-and-mix story—and Micron is investing aggressively to capture it:

• ~$27B of FY26 capex
• >$10B per quarter expected in FY27
• More than half the YoY increase tied to construction and clean-room capacity

Memory will remain cyclical. But the floor of the cycle may now be structurally higher.

Companies don’t invest tens of billions in new capacity because they expect demand to disappear.

text:
AI coding has a scaling problem nobody seems to be talking about.

AI is incredible at building software.

But the bigger the software gets, the more context the AI needs just to safely change it.

Eventually your architecture docs, business rules, decisions, dependencies, and specs become massive.

Then every fresh coding session has two choices:

🔥 Read everything → burn a ridiculous number of tokens before writing a line of code.

🎲 Read less → risk making a “correct” change that quietly breaks something elsewhere.

And here’s the part I think is even more dangerous:

The AI doesn’t know what it doesn’t know.

Tell an agent to modify Module A.

It reads everything about Module A.

Great.

Except Module A feeds Module F, shares a business rule with Module J, and changes a state that Module K depends on.

How does the AI know it needs to read F, J and K?

It can’t search for dependencies it doesn’t know exist.

So I’m experimenting with a different approach:

Stop giving AI the library. Give it the map.

A lightweight AI-readable index sits above the canonical documentation.

New session → small handoff → search the index → discover relevant concepts → follow dependencies → load only the canonical sections required → build.

In theory, you dramatically reduce token burn without sacrificing context.

But there’s a catch:

How do you build an index reliable enough to help the AI discover what it doesn’t know it needs—without the index itself becoming another monster that the AI has to read?

I think solving this becomes increasingly important as AI-built codebases get larger.

If you’re building serious software with AI, how are you solving this?

quotedTweet.text:
Building software is no longer my biggest problem. 🧐 

Getting the AI to remember how the software works is.

The codebase keeps growing but the AI’s required context is growing even faster…🤔

I’m looking for advice from people who have built large AI-assisted software projects.

As the project has grown, I’ve run into a problem that I didn’t anticipate: the software itself is becoming easier to manage than the AI context needed to build it.

Over time we’ve accumulated:

🔹Architecture documents
🔹Business rules
🔹Design decisions
🔹Development protocols
🔹Canonical specifications
🔹Historical decisions that can’t be forgotten

The result is a huge context that the AI needs to understand before it can safely make changes. Every new session feels like it has to relearn months of work.

This creates several problems:

🔹Context files become enormous.
🔹Startup time for a new session increases.
🔹Token usage (and cost) grows significantly.
🔹It becomes harder to know what context is actually necessary for a given task.
🔹There’s always the fear that leaving something out will cause the AI to make a change that violates an earlier design decision.

I’ve tried organizing documentation, splitting files into modules, maintaining canonical documents, and keeping decision logs, but the overall body of knowledge keeps growing.

For those of you building large AI-assisted codebases:

❓How do you keep context manageable?

❓Do you have a “context registry” or indexing system?

❓How do you decide what to load for a specific task?

❓Do you rely on retrieval (RAG), summaries, knowledge graphs, MCP servers, or something else?

❓Have you found a way to preserve architectural consistency without feeding hundreds of thousands of tokens into every new session?

I’m especially interested in hearing from teams building long-lived SaaS products where the AI has to understand not just code, but years of accumulated business logic and design decisions.

I’d love to hear what has worked and what hasn’t.

Building software is no longer my biggest problem. 🧐 

Getting the AI to remember how the software works is.

The codebase keeps growing but the AI’s required context is growing even faster…🤔

I’m looking for advice from people who have built large AI-assisted software projects.

As the project has grown, I’ve run into a problem that I didn’t anticipate: the software itself is becoming easier to manage than the AI context needed to build it.

Over time we’ve accumulated:

🔹Architecture documents
🔹Business rules
🔹Design decisions
🔹Development protocols
🔹Canonical specifications
🔹Historical decisions that can’t be forgotten

The result is a huge context that the AI needs to understand before it can safely make changes. Every new session feels like it has to relearn months of work.

This creates several problems:

🔹Context files become enormous.
🔹Startup time for a new session increases.
🔹Token usage (and cost) grows significantly.
🔹It becomes harder to know what context is actually necessary for a given task.
🔹There’s always the fear that leaving something out will cause the AI to make a change that violates an earlier design decision.

I’ve tried organizing documentation, splitting files into modules, maintaining canonical documents, and keeping decision logs, but the overall body of knowledge keeps growing.

For those of you building large AI-assisted codebases:

❓How do you keep context manageable?

❓Do you have a “context registry” or indexing system?

❓How do you decide what to load for a specific task?

❓Do you rely on retrieval (RAG), summaries, knowledge graphs, MCP servers, or something else?

❓Have you found a way to preserve architectural consistency without feeding hundreds of thousands of tokens into every new session?

I’m especially interested in hearing from teams building long-lived SaaS products where the AI has to understand not just code, but years of accumulated business logic and design decisions.

I’d love to hear what has worked and what hasn’t.

What do you mean you don’t know?

The scalp was in a Riker box, a display/specimen box  inside another box labeled “Indian Scalp.” A necklace made from Native American hand and foot bones was “hanging on a replica mantle display.”

This was in the Dan Beard exhibit at Bear Mountain, which had been on display since the 1940s. Now the official record says these are the physical remains of at least three Native American individuals, with the Stockbridge Munsee Community requesting transfer.

The issue is that the State of New York had some of the most horrifying post-contact human remains imaginable. 

PCurated, boxed, labeled, and displayed, and now claims it has no idea how they got there.

This is the same state apparatus that decides what counts as history, what counts as evidence, what counts as “cultural,”

Nobody should be shocked that the same people who tried to suppress a Paleoindian ceremonial landscape, an ocher mine, and a place anchored portable for years had a Native American scalp-and-bone necklace. It actually makes sense.  OPRHPs' “Our Whole History Initiative” doesn’t include Native Americans. 

This is to Jessica Vavrasek. Since you or anyone at OPRHP has no idea where, when, or how the scalp-and-bone necklace ended up in your exhibit, this would be a great place to start.

Global AI Secures $441 Million Financing to Accelerate Sovereign AI Infrastructure Expansion

@jpmorgan-led financing marks Global AI’s first debt raise and strengthens the company’s ability to deploy dedicated, single-tenant, air-gapped AI infrastructure for the world’s most sensitive workloads

NEW YORK, NY — [August 10th, 2026] — Global AI, the world’s first sovereign AI hyperscaler, today announced that it has closed $441 million in financing, marking the Company’s first-ever debt raise. 

The senior secured credit facility was led and arranged by J.P. Morgan, with participation from a group of leading lenders.

Founded in 2024, Global AI is purpose-built to design, build and operate dedicated, single-tenant, air-gapped AI infrastructure for the world’s most critical AI workloads. 

The company provides nations and enterprises with secure environments engineered for advanced AI training and inference, enabling customers to maintain control over their data, infrastructure and operations while benefiting from the scale, performance and operational sophistication of a hyperscaler.

Global AI Co-Founder, Director, and CEO Sami Issa said... 

“We are significantly accelerating our capital-raising efforts to meet the exceptional demand we are seeing for dedicated, single-tenant, air-gapped AI infrastructure. 

With $6.2 billion in contracted revenues, including $1 billion in contracted revenues already built and delivered to customers, we are scaling rapidly to meet this demand.”

Global AI is executing a significant expansion of its sovereign AI infrastructure platform across the United States and expects to have 1 GW of capacity available by 2029.

About Global AI
-----------------
Global AI is a U.S.-based, vertically integrated sovereign AI infrastructure company and the world’s first sovereign AI hyperscaler, designing, building, powering, and operating dedicated, single-tenant, air-gapped AI data centers that enable nations and enterprises to develop and deploy artificial intelligence within their own jurisdiction.

Global AI’s fully integrated model spans land, energy, construction, advanced liquid cooling, and GPU-dense compute, providing physical and operational separation across the entire AI infrastructure stack. 

With infrastructure deployments across the United States, Global AI is executing a disciplined expansion strategy toward 1 gigawatt of critical capacity by the end of 2029, delivering secure, compliant, and sovereign AI infrastructure at national scale.

Introducing EB Core — a Persistent AI Operational Intelligence Layer.

Most AI systems are good at conversation, but weak at operating inside real business workflows. EB Core is built for the harder problem: turning messy natural language into persistent structured operational state.

That state controls grounding, constraint persistence, identity-aware interpretation, refusal, explainability, and safe execution boundaries.

Video 1: Cinematic overview
Video 2: Live proof demo inside EasyBuy

EB Core is demonstrated inside EasyBuy, a live commerce app with 50K+ Play Store downloads, and is being extended through a public Operational Intelligence Playground covering commerce, support ops, logistics, finance ops, and healthcare admin simulations.

Same architecture. Different operational domains.

Not a chatbot.
Not a prompt wrapper.
Not just ecommerce search.

Persistent Operational Intelligence for AI.

Open to technical feedback from builders, engineers, investors, and the xAI community.
